chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Munqari, from Yunus ibn Zabyan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Why do you not forbid these two men from this man?' He said: 'Who is this man, and who are these two men?' I said: 'Why do you not forbid Hujr ibn Zaydah and Amr ibn Jud'ah from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar?' He said: 'O Yunus! I had asked them both to refrain from it, but they did not do so. So I summoned them, and asked them, and wrote to them, and made it my need from them, but they did not refrain from it. So may Allah not forgive them both. By Allah, Al-Kuthayyir 'Uzzah is more truthful in his friendship than they are in what they claim of friendship with me, where he said: 'Does she not claim by the unseen that I do not love her? If I were not honored by her noble one, [I would not love her].' By Allah, if they both loved me, they would love the one whom I love.'

key_terms.أَلْكَثَيِّرُ عَزَّةَ: Al-Kuthayyir 'Uzzah (a poet known for his love for the Prophet's family)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq not forbid his companions from criticizing Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reveals that his restraint in forbidding Hujr ibn Zaydah and Amr ibn Jud'a from criticizing Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar stems from their persistent refusal to heed his repeated verbal and written requests, rather than a lack of authority. He employs the poetic metaphor of Al-Kuthayyir 'Uzzah to illustrate the Shia criterion of *al-wala'* (loyalty), arguing that true affection for the Imam necessitates loving his chosen companions, a trait these men superficially claim but fail to embody. This narration underscores the scholarly principle that the Imam's silence or specific actions often serve as a nuanced indicator of the spiritual standing and sincerity of his followers.

en.hubeali: H 15008 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al-Husayn Bin Saeed, together from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Husayn Bin Ahmad Al-Munqary, from Yunus Bin Zabyaan who said:

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, Why do youasws not forbid these two men from (criticising) this man?’ So heasws said: ‘Who is this man, and who are these two men?’ I said, ‘Why do youasws not forbid Hujr Bin Zaida, and Aamir Bin Juza’at, from (criticising) Al-Mufazzal Bin Umar?’ So heasws said: ‘O Yunus! Iasws had asked these two to refrain from it, but they did not do it. So I called the two of them over, and asked both of them, and wrote to both of them telling them what Iasws needed from both of them, but they still did not restrain themselves from it. So, may Allahazwj not Forgive them both, for by Allahazwj, there are many honourable ones in his cordiality than these two regarding what they are impersonating from myasws cordiality. Where he has said, ‘Why does she think by the absence that I do not love her?’, then the two of them have not honoured measws, but by Allahazwj, had they both loved measws, they would have loved the one whom Iasws love’.
en.sarwar: 562. Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al-Nu’man, from Al-Qasim the associate of Al-Mufazzal, and he was a truthful man, who said: ‘I heard Abu Abdullah (a.s.) saying: ‘There is a group in the Masjid who publicise us (a.s.) and publicise themselves.

They are neither from us (a.s.) nor are we (a.s.) from them. I (a.s.) rush away and hide, but they still uncover my (a.s.) veil. May Allah (azwj) violate their veil. They are saying that I (a.s.) am the Imam (a.s.), but, by Allah (azwj), I (a.s.) am not an Imam (a.s.) except for the one who obeys me (a.s.). So as for the one who disobeys me (a.s.), I (a.s.) am not an Imam (a.s.) for him. Why are they attaching themselves to my (a.s.) name, and not refraining from mentioning my (a.s.) name from their mouths? By Allah (azwj), may He (azwj) not Gather me (a.s.) and them in one abode’.
